0.content:
# Airflow Run-Level Drill-Down (Metrics + Traces) — Dynatrace Dashboard

Third companion to `01-airflow-fleet-metrics.json` and `02-airflow-dag-level.json`. Environment: Airflow 3.x, OTLP **metrics + traces** both on (`otel_prefix="airflow"`), hybrid **CeleryExecutor + KubernetesExecutor**, **Edge workers** in use, **OpenLineage** enabled, ~200+ DAGs / high concurrency, Grail/DQL available (built entirely as `timeseries` (metrics) / `fetch spans` (traces) DQL tiles, no classic metric-selector tiles and no `fetch metrics`).

**Why this dashboard is split into stages:** `airflow.*` metrics carry `dag_id`/`task_id` but **never `run_id`** — there is no metric-side key to jump straight to "this specific run." Traces (root span `dag_run.{dag_id}`, attributes `airflow.dag_id` + `airflow.dag_run.run_id`/`airflow.run_id`) are the only signal with run-level granularity. So: Section 1 uses metrics to spot *roughly when* something went wrong for a `dag_id`; Section 2 uses traces to resolve the exact `run_id` in that window; Section 3 drills into that one trace; Section 4 cross-references metrics for the same DAG over the run's approximate time window as a best-effort (not guaranteed 1:1) sanity check.

**Variables:** `dag_id` (single-select — this dashboard is meant for one DAG at a time) → `run_id` (single-select, populated from distinct `airflow.dag_run.run_id`/`airflow.run_id` values seen on **trace root spans** for the selected `dag_id`, since it cannot be resolved from metrics) → hidden helper variables `run_start`/`run_end` (populated from the selected run's root span, used to scope Section 4's metrics query to that run's time window — see REVIEW note in Section 4).

**REVIEW — could not confirm from the prompt/spec, verify before relying on this dashboard:**
- Whether `task_span_detail_level` is enabled (sub-step spans nested under `task_run`) — Section 3 includes a nested-spans tile for this, but it will simply return empty if the feature is off.
- Whether `dagrun_parent_trace_context` is used to nest Airflow's trace inside an upstream system's trace — if so, this DAG's `dag_run.{dag_id}` span will not be the true trace root (`parent.span.id` will be non-null, pointing to the upstream span), which breaks the `isNull(parent.span.id)` root-detection used throughout this dashboard. The `matchesValue(span.name, "dag_run.*")` fallback is included specifically to cover this case, but confirm which detection actually fires on your tenant.
- Typical concurrent-run count per DAG — if a single `dag_id` regularly has multiple runs in flight, treat Section 4's time-window cross-check as approximate (it is explicitly labeled as such) since it cannot distinguish overlapping runs of the same DAG.
- Exact field name for the parent-span reference: Dynatrace sources disagree between `parent.span.id` and `span.parent_id`; this dashboard uses `parent.span.id` (matches Dynatrace's own trace/span field-naming convention) — confirm against a live `fetch spans` query on your tenant and adjust every tile below if it differs.
- Exact attribute key prefix for the task_run-level attributes (`try_number`, `map_index`, `hostname`, `operator`, `pool`, `job_id`, `log_url`, `executor_state`) — the traces spec lists these without consistently repeating the `airflow.` prefix. This dashboard assumes `airflow.try_number`, `airflow.map_index`, etc. (consistent namespacing with `airflow.task_id`/`airflow.dag_id`) — confirm and adjust field names in Section 3 if your exporter emits them unprefixed.

1.content:
## 1. Anomaly Timeline (metrics, filtered by `dag_id`)

> Same underlying signals as `02-airflow-dag-level.json`, purpose-built here to spot *roughly when/where* something went wrong so you can hand off a time range to Section 2. All tiles filtered by `dag_id` only (metrics have no `run_id`).

2.title: DAG run duration — success vs failed (p50/p90/max)
2.subtitle: Primary "something changed here" signal. Click/zoom into the anomalous region, then note the timestamp for Section 2. Timer metric — requires OTLP exponential-histogram support for accurate percentiles.

3.title: Schedule delay
3.subtitle: Sustained p90 above ~5 min (tune to this DAG's schedule interval) suggests scheduler contention rather than a single bad run.

4.title: Task failures over time, by task_id (top 20 by failure count)
4.query: timeseries failures=sum(airflow.ti_failures), filter: in(dag_id, $dag_id), by:{task_id} | sort arrayAvg(failures[]) desc | limit 20
4.subtitle: Which task(s) started failing and when. Top-20-by-failures limit is a cardinality guard at 200+ DAGs; widen if a DAG has more failing tasks than that.

5.content: **→ Next step:** note the approximate timestamp (or zoom the dashboard timeframe to the narrow window) where the anomaly above appears, then scroll to **Section 2** below and use that same dashboard timeframe to resolve the exact `run_id`.

6.content:
## 2. Run Lookup (traces, filtered by `dag_id` + the dashboard timeframe)

> Lists `dag_run.{dag_id}` root spans in the current dashboard timeframe so you can resolve which `run_id` corresponds to the anomaly spotted in Section 1. Narrow the dashboard's global timeframe to the window from Section 1 before reading this table.

**Limitation (flagging rather than guessing):** raw Dynatrace dashboard JSON does not support "click a table row to set a dashboard variable" as a built-in tile interaction — the `run_id` variable above is populated by its own query (same root-span filter, distinct `run_id` values) and is selected manually from its dropdown. This table's job is to show you *which* `run_id` to pick (sorted so failed/abnormally-long runs surface first) and to give you the exact value to paste in if it isn't in the dropdown yet (e.g. dropdown result-count cap).

7.title: Root dag_run spans for this DAG in the current timeframe (failed/abnormal first)
7.query: fetch spans | filter airflow.dag_id == $dag_id and (isNull(parent.span.id) or matchesValue(span.name, "dag_run.*")) | fieldsAdd run_id = coalesce(airflow.dag_run.run_id, airflow.run_id) | fieldsAdd duration_s = duration / 1e9 | fieldsAdd outcome = if(status.code == "STATUS_CODE_ERROR", "failed", else: "success") | fields run_id, start_time, duration_s, outcome, trace.id | sort outcome asc, duration_s desc | limit 200
7.subtitle: REVIEW: root-span detection uses isNull(parent.span.id) with a span.name fallback for setups using dagrun_parent_trace_context (see header note). Sort puts "failed" before "success" alphabetically, then longest duration first within each group.

8.content:
## 3. Run Inspector (traces, filtered by `dag_id` + `run_id`)

> Once `run_id` is set above, everything below drills into that one trace: every child `task_run` span in execution order, with duration, offset from run start, status, and the task-level attributes needed to jump to logs or spot retries.

9.title: Total run duration
9.query: fetch spans | filter airflow.dag_id == $dag_id and coalesce(airflow.dag_run.run_id, airflow.run_id) == $run_id and (isNull(parent.span.id) or matchesValue(span.name, "dag_run.*")) | fieldsAdd duration_s = duration / 1e9 | fields duration_s | limit 1
9.subtitle: Root dag_run span duration, in seconds.

10.title: Total task_run span count
10.query: fetch spans | filter airflow.dag_id == $dag_id and coalesce(airflow.dag_run.run_id, airflow.run_id) == $run_id and isNotNull(parent.span.id) | summarize task_span_count = count()
10.subtitle: All descendant spans of the run (task_run spans plus any nested sub-step spans, if task_span_detail_level is on).

11.content: **How big was this run** — pair the two stat tiles above with the waterfall table to the right/below: a large task-span count relative to a short total duration usually means high fan-out/parallelism; a long total duration with few task spans usually means a serial critical path or one slow task.

12.title: task_run span waterfall (execution order)
12.query: fetch spans | filter airflow.dag_id == $dag_id and coalesce(airflow.dag_run.run_id, airflow.run_id) == $run_id | lookup [fetch spans | filter airflow.dag_id == $dag_id and coalesce(airflow.dag_run.run_id, airflow.run_id) == $run_id and (isNull(parent.span.id) or matchesValue(span.name, "dag_run.*")) | fields root_span_id = span.id, run_start_time = start_time], sourceField: airflow.dag_id, lookupField: airflow.dag_id | filter parent.span.id == root_span_id | fieldsAdd start_offset_s = (start_time - run_start_time) / 1e9 | fieldsAdd duration_s = duration / 1e9 | fieldsAdd outcome = if(status.code == "STATUS_CODE_ERROR", "error", else: "ok") | fieldsAdd is_retry = airflow.try_number > 0 | fields task_id = airflow.task_id, try_number = airflow.try_number, map_index = airflow.map_index, hostname = airflow.hostname, operator = airflow.operator, pool = airflow.pool, job_id = airflow.job_id, log_url = airflow.log_url, executor_state = airflow.executor_state, start_offset_s, duration_s, outcome, is_retry | sort start_offset_s asc | limit 500
12.subtitle: Row per direct child span of the root (task_run level). Rows highlighted red are status=error; orange are try_number > 0 (a retry). log_url renders as a link-out to the task's Airflow logs. REVIEW: attribute prefix assumption for try_number/map_index/hostname/operator/pool/job_id/log_url/executor_state — see header note. This dashboard-JSON format does not support an inline collapsible waterfall/Gantt visualization; table sorted by start_offset_s is the closest DQL-tile equivalent — use the Distributed Traces app (linked from the trace.id in Section 2) for a true visual waterfall if your edition includes it.

13.content: **Nested sub-step spans** (below) only return rows if `task_span_detail_level` is enabled on this deployment — confirmed as unspecified in this project's setup notes (see header REVIEW). If it's off, this table will simply be empty; that's expected, not a broken query.

14.title: Nested sub-step spans within each task_run (if task_span_detail_level is enabled)
14.query: fetch spans | filter airflow.dag_id == $dag_id and coalesce(airflow.dag_run.run_id, airflow.run_id) == $run_id and isNotNull(parent.span.id) | lookup [fetch spans | filter airflow.dag_id == $dag_id and coalesce(airflow.dag_run.run_id, airflow.run_id) == $run_id and (isNull(parent.span.id) or matchesValue(span.name, "dag_run.*")) | fields root_span_id = span.id], sourceField: airflow.dag_id, lookupField: airflow.dag_id | filter parent.span.id != root_span_id | fieldsAdd duration_s = duration / 1e9 | fieldsAdd outcome = if(status.code == "STATUS_CODE_ERROR", "error", else: "ok") | fields span.name, parent.span.id, task_id = airflow.task_id, duration_s, outcome, start_time | sort start_time asc | limit 500
14.subtitle: Any span whose parent is not the root — i.e. nested under a task_run span. Grouped by the task_id it inherits and parent.span.id so you can see which task_run each sub-step belongs to.

15.content:
## 4. Cross-Check Against Metrics For the Same Run (best-effort correlation)

> **Metrics cannot be filtered by `run_id`.** This section narrows `airflow.task.*` metrics for this `dag_id` to the exact time window covered by the selected trace (`run_start` → `run_end`, populated from the root span above) as an approximate per-task timing cross-reference against what the trace shows.
>
> **This is a time-window approximation, not a guaranteed 1:1 join.** At 200+ DAGs with high concurrency, if this `dag_id` has more than one run in flight during that window, the metrics below reflect *all* overlapping runs of this DAG, not only the selected one — read the trace-based numbers in Section 3 as ground truth for this specific run and use this section only to sanity-check they're in the same ballpark.

16.title: Task duration / scheduled / queued, by task_id, narrowed to this run's time window
16.query: timeseries p50=percentile(airflow.task.duration,50), p90=percentile(airflow.task.duration,90), schedP90=percentile(airflow.task.scheduled_duration,90), queuedP90=percentile(airflow.task.queued_duration,90), filter: in(dag_id, $dag_id), by:{task_id}, from:$run_start, to:$run_end | sort p90 desc | limit 50
16.subtitle: REVIEW: from:/to: bound to the run_start/run_end helper variables, which hold raw epoch values pulled from the trace's start_time/duration fields. Confirm your DQL version accepts variable-substituted epoch values directly in timeseries from:/to: — if not, read run_start/run_end from Section 3's stat tiles and set the dashboard's global timeframe to that window manually instead. Timer metrics — require OTLP exponential-histogram support for accurate percentiles.

17.content:
## Setup Notes (verify before trusting this dashboard — not a live tile)

- Confirm `[traces] otel_on = True` is set — this is a **separate config block** from `[metrics] otel_on`; having metrics flowing does not mean traces are.
- Confirm `otel_host`, `otel_port`, and `otel_ssl_active` under `[traces]` are configured and point at Dynatrace's **trace/span ingest endpoint**, which is not necessarily the same endpoint/port as the metrics OTLP receiver — verify both pipelines independently rather than assuming one implies the other.
- Confirm the OTLP traces pipeline is actually reaching Dynatrace (a quick `fetch spans | filter airflow.dag_id == "<any known dag>" | limit 1` returning rows is the fastest check) before relying on Sections 2–4 of this dashboard.
- This dashboard assumes Grail/DQL is available on this tenant (confirmed in this project's environment notes) so all trace tiles are built as inline `fetch spans` DQL tiles. If a future tenant/edition doesn't support `fetch spans` in dashboard tiles, substitute Section 2/3's tiles with markdown tiles linking out to the Distributed Traces app, filtered by `dag_id`/`trace.id`, instead.
- See the dashboard header (top of page) for the full list of unconfirmed attribute names and detection logic (root-span identification, attribute prefixing, `task_span_detail_level`, `dagrun_parent_trace_context`) that should be validated against a live query before this dashboard is treated as production-ready.
